knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The procedure says to plan loads and movement before lifting, use carts and break up repetitive work, and assess the route and load.
The lesson says to stop when the load or route is beyond safe capability, to request assistance for awkward loads and to avoid twisting under load.
The worked scenario says the cleaner assesses the load, route and safer transport arrangements before proceeding. Carrying heavy loads by leaning back or twisting is unsafe.

Carrying two full buckets up the stairs at once is the unsafe alternative. The lesson says to avoid twisting under load, and carts, breaks and help are the safer options. Using a cart on suitable ground, keeping loads close to the body and breaking up repetitive work are all safe practices.

Reporting a task that is beyond personal capacity so that a safer system can be arranged is correct. The assessor checks that the worker reports tasks beyond personal capacity, and a task-risk review is completed before work. Keeping the excess load to yourself, asking a client to lift or recording nothing are not acceptable.

practicalCriteria: Chooses safer systems and reports tasks beyond personal capacity.
Explains applicable scope and site procedures
Demonstrates hazard controls and safe stop-work decisions
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 3: Keep loads close to the body, and avoid twisting while carrying a load.
Record of procedure step 6: Report any task that is beyond your personal capacity, and agree a safer system of work with the supervisor.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 6 is not done: Report any task that is beyond your personal capacity, and agree a safer system of work with the supervisor.
Stop work if procedure step 7 is not done: Do not rely on one lifting posture as a guarantee against injury; choose the method for the task and the worker.
